answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated service capacity at a global registrar to maintain a unique identity, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent must traverse a spiral of time-gated slots, treating its tenure as a comet of recorded activity. A verifier monitors for wander attempts across partitions; any overlap results in a permanent prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal costs.
